questions.question_purpose: Classify variables and explain what grouping loses.
questions.context: A college records travel mode, number of bus changes and journey time in minutes for each student. Journey time is rounded to the nearest minute.

questions.question_purpose: Calculate location and choose a robust summary.
questions.context: The waiting times, in minutes, of seven customers are shown. Treat them as the complete set of observations.

Q2(c): justification referring to 30 minutes and influence on mean

questions.question_purpose: Estimate summaries from grouped data and explain their meaning.
questions.context: A technician groups the download times t, in seconds, for 40 files. Use class midpoints for the estimated mean. Use position 0.75n and linear interpolation for the 75th percentile.

Q3(a): correct weighted midpoint sum divided by 40
Q3(b): interpolation or correct cumulative-frequency boundary giving 20

questions.question_purpose: Calculate spread and apply an explicitly specified outlier rule.
questions.context: Twelve packet delivery times in minutes are ordered below. Define Q1 and Q3 as the medians of the lower six and upper six values. Use the rule: an outlier lies below Q1 - 1.5 IQR or above Q3 + 1.5 IQR.

questions.question_purpose: Use both location and variation to make a contextual comparison.
questions.context: A student samples 30 comparable weekday journeys on each of two routes. The table summarises journey times in minutes.

Q5(b): summaries do not give all values/extremes

questions.question_purpose: Connect summary statistics, variance, standard deviation and units.
questions.context: For eight measured fill volumes x in millilitres, n = 8, sum x = 400 and sum x^2 = 20072. Describe these eight observations using divisor n, not n - 1.

Q6(c): second machine less variable with SD evidence
SD is not a maximum deviation or guarantee

questions.question_purpose: Analyse weather data with an explicit cleaning policy and qualified conclusions.
questions.context: ILLUSTRATIVE DATA: these invented values are not Pearson LDS observations. Daily rainfall at fictional Station P over six scheduled days is 0, 1.2, tr, 0, 4.8, missing (mm). Here tr means 0 < rainfall < 0.05 mm. For this calculation replace tr by 0. Station R has a reported mean of 0.8 mm over six complete days in a different month.

Q7(b): missing day cannot be treated as zero

questions.question_purpose: Combine an updated mean with an evaluation of an unjustified conclusion.
questions.context: In a second delivery study, 10 recorded times have mean 18 minutes. One time is 54 minutes. A comparable service has mean 15 minutes. The analyst proposes removing 54 because it makes the first service look slow.

Q8(b): valid data-quality reason needed for removal
